statement.notation: RK(X), ∃-ISO(X), ∃-EMB(X), COMP(X), EQU=ISO(X), WQO(X) for X ∈ {On, WFT, SABA, R-p-G, CCS}
statement.name: Statements about ranked structures (ordinals, well-founded trees, superatomic Boolean algebras, reduced Abelian p-groups, countable compact spaces)
statement.definition: RK: every structure in the class is ranked. ∃-ISO: for a sequence of structures in the class, the set of isomorphic pairs exists. ∃-EMB: the same for embeddability. COMP: any two structures are comparable under embeddability. EQU=ISO: mutual embeddability implies isomorphism. WQO: the class is a well-quasi-order under embeddability.
statement.facts: Almost all of these statements (for On, WFT, SABA, R-p-G, CCS) are equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 or ACA0. Exceptions: ∃-ISO(WFT) follows from ATR0 and implies it. EQU=ISO is false for WFT and R-p-G. COMP is false for R-p-G. In every class the statements imply ACA0 (or IΣ2 for WQO) over RCA0. The reductions are from On to the other classes by computable transformations, from WFT, SABA and R-p-G to On by EW reductions, and ATR0 shows that every structure of each class is ranked.

statement.notation: EW and computable (c, ec) reductions between classes
statement.name: Effective Wadge and computable-transformation reductions
statement.definition: X1 ≤EW X2 if a computable functional Φ satisfies Φ^{-1}X2 = X1. X1 ≤c X2 if there is a computable transformation preserving isomorphism and non-isomorphism. X1 ≤ec X2 if the transformation preserves both embeddability and non-embeddability.
statement.facts: On ≤EW,c every other class over RCA0, and On ≤EW,c,ec over ACA0. Over ATR0, WFT ≤EW,ec On, SABA ≤EW,c,ec On and R-p-G ≤EW On. R-p-G ≰ec On.

statement.notation: Hyperarithmetic versus recursive up to equimorphism (Theorems 1.9-1.11)
statement.name: Every hyperarithmetic structure is equimorphic/isomorphic to a recursive one
statement.definition: Classical computability results for trees, Boolean algebras, compact metric spaces and Abelian p-groups.
statement.facts: Every hyperarithmetic tree or Boolean algebra is equimorphic to a recursive one. Every hyperarithmetic compact metric space is isomorphic to a computable one. Every hyperarithmetic Abelian p-group is equimorphic to a recursive one.

statement.name: Π01-generic approximation principle
statement.definition: For any uniformly Π01 collection of dense sets of strings D_i there is a sequence g_0,g_1,... of reals with (∀i)(∃m)(∃t)(∀u>t)[g_u↾m = g_t↾m ∈ D_i].
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0 + IΣ02 (Thm 3.2); RCA0 + BΣ02 + Π01GA proves IΣ02 (Thm 3.3); implied by Π01G, hence Π11-conservative over RCA0 and does not imply BΣ02; AMT does not imply it (Cor. 3.4). It is the key principle in Figure 2 for entries marked 3 and 4.

statement.name: Π0n generic approximation (and Π0nG)
statement.definition: Approximations in the sense of the iterated limit lemma to generics for uniformly Π0n sequences of dense sets of strings.
statement.facts: RCA0 + IΣ0n+1 proves Π0nGA (Thm A.1); RCA0 + BΣ0n+1 + Π0nGA proves IΣ0n+1 (Thm A.2); Π0nG is Π11-conservative (indeed restricted Π12-conservative) over RCA0.

statement.name: Atomic Tree Theorem
statement.definition: If T is an atomic extendible tree, then there is a listing of the isolated paths of T.
statement.facts: ATT implies AMT; provable from Π01G and from RCA0 + BΣ02 + AMT; restricted Π12-conservative over RCA0 and Π11-conservative over RCA0 + BΣ02. Open whether AMT implies ATT.

statement.name: Finite Atomic Tree Theorem
statement.definition: For an atomic extendible tree and finitely many nodes there are isolated paths extending each of them.
statement.facts: Follows from BΣ02 and from ATT; not provable in RCA0 (Thm B.2). Open whether Π01GA implies it.

statement.name: ATT with strengthened hypothesis
statement.definition: An extendible tree satisfying the conclusion of FATT has a listing of its isolated paths.
statement.facts: Intermediate between ATT and AMT; no results proved.

statement.name: Homogeneous Model Theorem
statement.definition: For a theory T and a list X of types satisfying the finite full amalgamation closure conditions there is a homogeneous model A with T(A) = X.
statement.facts: Equivalent to AMT over RCA0 (Thm 7.6) and uniformly (Weihrauch) equivalent to AMT (Thm 7.11); HMT-bounding degrees coincide with AMT-bounding degrees (Cor. 7.12).

statement.name: Weak Model Existence Theorem
statement.definition: For a theory T and a list X of types satisfying the finite free amalgamation closure conditions there is a model A with T(A) = X.
statement.facts: Equivalent to AMT over RCA0 (Thm 7.6); uniformly equivalent to AMT (Thm 7.11).

statement.name: 1-Point Homogeneous Model Theorem
statement.definition: Analogue of HMT with 1-point full amalgamation closure conditions and 1-point homogeneous models.
statement.facts: Equivalent to AMT + IΣ02 over RCA0 (Thm 7.7).

statement.name: 1-Homogeneous Model Theorem; Strong Model Existence Theorem
statement.definition: HMT-style statements with pairwise full amalgamation (1-homogeneous models), resp. pairwise free amalgamation (arbitrary models).
statement.facts: Each implies AMT over RCA0 (Thm 7.8); provable in RCA0 + ATT + Π01GA (Thm 7.9); not provable in RCA0 + ATT + BΣ02 (Thm 7.10); exact strength open.

statement.name: Extension function approximation existence under closure conditions C
statement.definition: Every list of types satisfying closure conditions C has an extension function approximation.
statement.facts: For finite full or finite free amalgamation, equivalent to AMT over RCA0; for pairwise full, pairwise free or 1-point full, implies AMT and is implied by ATT (Thm 7.5).

statement.name: Variants of homogeneity and implications between them
statement.definition: Four classically equivalent definitions of homogeneous model and the principles that every model with one property has another.
statement.facts: 1-point homogeneous ⇒ 1-homogeneous is equivalent to IΣ02 (Thm 4.3); 1-homogeneous ⇒ homogeneous and strongly 1-homogeneous ⇒ homogeneous are equivalent to BΣ02 (Thm 4.4); homogeneous ⇒ strongly 1-homogeneous implies ACA0 (Prop 4.2); models with the same type spectrum being isomorphic is equivalent to ACA0 (Prop 4.7).

statement.name: Closure conditions on lists of types and model existence from extension function approximations
statement.definition: Statements about lists of types satisfying pairwise, finite or 1-point, free or full amalgamation and the existence of listings or models with prescribed type spectrum.
statement.facts: Various equivalent to IΣ02 or BΣ02 over RCA0, provable in RCA0, or sandwiched via Π01GA as summarized in Figure 2.

statement.name: Arithmetical transfinite induction schemes and restricted transfinite induction/least element schemes
statement.definition: Transfinite induction along a well ordering α for arithmetical formulas (ATI0), and versions restricted to Σ⁰ₖ or Π⁰ₖ formulas, together with transfinite least element schemes.
statement.facts: Theorem 39: RCA0 proves Π⁰₁-TI0 and Σ⁰₁-TLE0. Theorem 40: for j ≥ 2 and k ≥ 1, over RCA0 the following are equivalent to ACA0: ATI0, Σ⁰ₖ-TI0, Π⁰ₖ-TLE0, Π⁰ⱼ-TI0, Σ⁰ⱼ-TLE0.

statement.name: Sherman's inequality for ordinal multiplication
statement.definition: For well orderings α, β, γ: (α+β)γ ≤ αγ + βγ.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Theorem 24).

statement.notation: Σ¹₁-AC0 bounded version; no descending sequence of well orderings
statement.name: No infinite strictly descending sequence of well orderings
statement.definition: There is no sequence ⟨αᵢ⟩ of well orderings with αᵢ₊₁ <w αᵢ for all i.
statement.facts: Over ACA0 it is equivalent to Σ¹₁-AC0 (Theorem 5). The finite-length version (transitivity of <w along finite chains) is equivalent to bounded Σ¹₁-AC0 over ACA0 (Theorem 6).

statement.name: Well-orderedness of α^β and 2^α
statement.definition: If α and β are well ordered then so is α^β; if α is well ordered then so is 2^α.
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Variants of the ATR problem
statement.definition: Versions of ATR iterating an arbitrary arithmetical operator, taking a labeled well-ordering, or asking for a single column Y_c of a hierarchy.

statement.name: Hierarchy with X_a' ≤T X_b for a<b
statement.definition: Given a well-ordering L and A, produce <X_a> with X_{0_L}=A and X_a' ≤T X_b for all a<_L b.
statement.facts: The Turing jump problem, and hence ATR, is not Weihrauch reducible to it; ATR is arithmetically Weihrauch reducible to it.

statement.name: Variants of ATR2
statement.definition: Two-sided ATR for arbitrary arithmetical operators, for labeled linear orderings, and with the weak hierarchy condition X_a' ≤T X_b.

statement.name: Jullien's theorem (essential segment formulation)
statement.definition: A scattered linear ordering is extendible iff it has no essential segment of the form 2 or R+Q with R indecomposable to the right and Q indecomposable to the left.
statement.facts: The left-to-right direction is provable in RCA0. JUL implies FRA over RCA0. FRA plus Σ¹₁-IND implies JUL; JUL and FRA are equivalent over RCA0 + Σ¹₁-IND.

statement.name: Signed trees are well quasi-ordered
statement.definition: Every sequence of well-founded {+,-}-labelled trees has i<j with a homomorphism from T_i to T_j.
statement.facts: Equivalent to FRA and FINDEC over RCA0 (Theorem 4.2, Corollary 3.7). Implies ATR0 over RCA0 (Proposition 2.14). Follows from FRA.

statement.name: Finite decomposability of scattered linear orderings
statement.definition: Every scattered linear ordering is equimorphic to a finite sum of h-indecomposable linear orderings.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to WQO(ST) and FRA, and to the existence of minimal decompositions of scattered linear orderings (Corollary 3.11). Implies ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Jullien's theorem via minimal decompositions
statement.definition: For a minimal decomposition F_0..F_n of L, L is extendible iff no F_i=F_{i+1}=1 and no F_i indecomposable to the right followed by F_{i+1} indecomposable to the left.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR* (ATR0 + Σ¹₁-IND) over RCA0 + Σ¹₁-IND (Theorem 5.14). The left-to-right direction is provable in RCA0.

statement.notation: extendibility of ω*, ζ, η, ω^2, h-indecomposables
statement.name: Extendibility of linear orderings
statement.definition: A linear ordering L is extendible if every countable partial ordering not embedding L has a linearization not embedding L.
statement.facts: ATR* proves extendibility of ω*, (ω²)*, η and every h-indecomposable linear ordering (Theorems 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 6.20), with hyperarithmetic linearizations. Extendibility of ζ implies ATR0 (cited DHLS03).

statement.name: Fan Theorem (intuitionistic)
statement.definition: Every bar in Cantor space 2^ω decided by a sequence has a finite subset that is a bar; formulated in the intuitionistic system BIM.
statement.facts: Proved equivalent in BIM to the Heine-Borel theorem HB (Theorem 3.5), to Sigma^0_1-BI for Cantor space (Theorem 3.1), and to the thin-bar-finite formulation (Theorem 3.4). Implied by OI([0,1]) (via Theorem 4.2 and Theorem 3.5).

statement.name: Principle of Open Induction on [0,1]
statement.definition: Every open subset H of R that is progressive in [0,1] contains [0,1].
statement.facts: BIM proves Sigma^0_1-BI → OI([0,1]) and OI([0,1]) → HB. BIM proves OI([0,1]) equivalent to OI(2^ω), to the contrapositive of Dedekind's theorem, to EnDec?! and to WFKB. BIM + FT does not prove OI([0,1]). OI([0,1]) + IRT(2) → AppFT. With MP1: OI([0,1]) ↔ AppFT ↔ Sigma^0_1-ND ↔ AlmFT.

statement.name: Approximate-Fan Theorem
statement.definition: In an explicit approximate fan every thin bar is almost-finite.
statement.facts: BIM proves BI → AppFT. BIM proves AppFT ↔ contrapositive of Bolzano-Weierstrass ↔ Ascoli lemma contrapositive ↔ IRT ↔ IRT(3) ↔ SemiappFT. AppFT → OI([0,1]). AppFT extends FT. BIM + FT does not prove AppFT.

statement.name: Intuitionistic Ramsey Theorem
statement.definition: For decidable subsets of omega, the intersection of two k-almost-full sets is k-almost-full.
statement.facts: BIM proves IRT ↔ IRT(3) ↔ AppFT. BIM proves IRT → Paris-Harrington PH. CRT(1) implies LPO.

statement.name: Bar Induction on Baire space
statement.definition: If B is a monotone and inductive bar in omega^omega, then the empty sequence is in B.
statement.facts: BIM proves Sigma^0_1-BI → OI([0,1]); Pi^1_1-BI → AlmFT; BI → AppFT.

statement.name: Totalizing jump
statement.definition: tJ(f)(e,i,p) = {Φ_i(p,q) : q ∈ fΦ_e(p)} if Φ_e(p) ∈ dom(f) and Φ_i(p,q) converges for all such q; otherwise tJ(f)(e,i,p) = N^N. This is an operator on problems and is not the Turing jump TJ.
statement.facts: tJ induces a jump operator on the Weihrauch degrees: f <W tJ(f), and f ≤W g implies tJ(f) ≤W tJ(g) (Theorem 3.4). tJ is injective on the degrees (Theorem 3.7). tJ(f) ≡W T h for some h ≡W f (Theorem 3.3). tJ(f) is total and join-irreducible but never a cylinder. tJ(∅) ≡W id. tJ(id) ≡W χ_{Π02→Π01}, with LPO <W tJ(id) <W tJ(id)^ ≡W lim. tJ(id) ≰W TC_N. tJ(C_N) ≡W T(C_N × W_{Π02→Π01}). tJ(C_{2^N}) ≡W T(C_{2^N} × W_{Π02→Π01}). tJ(lim^[n]) ≡W T(lim^[n]). tJ(UC_{N^N}) ≡W TUC_{N^N} and tJ(C_{N^N}) ≡W TC_{N^N}. C_N, C_{2^N}, DIS, LPO and TC_N are not in the range of tJ. There is no f with TC_N ≡W tJ(f). The n-th iterate tJ^n(id) is characterized by g_n (Theorem 4.5).

statement.name: Addresses of infinitely many zeroes
statement.definition: W_{Π02→Π01}(p) is the set of strictly increasing q with p∘q = 0^N, i.e. a list of the positions of infinitely many zeroes of p; partial and uniformly computable.
statement.facts: tJ(f) ≡W T(W ∗ f ∗ W) (Theorem 3.10). For some f, both tJ(f) ≰W T(W ∗ f) and tJ(f) ≰W T(f ∗ W) (Proposition 3.11).

statement.name: Π02-to-Π01 question transformer (isFiniteS)
statement.definition: χ(p) = {q : (∃∞ n) p(n)=0 ⇔ (∀n) q(n)=0}, a total problem equivalent to Neumann–Pauly's isFiniteS.
statement.facts: χ ≡W T(W_{Π02→Π01}) (Proposition 4.3). tJ(id) ≡W χ (Theorem 4.4). χ ≰W TC_N, citing [17, Prop. 24(5)].

statement.name: n-fold serial Σ02-question problem
statement.definition: g_n(p) lists the solutions of the form 0^{σ(0)}1^{σ(1)}...m^{σ(m-1)}m^N, where m is the least number occurring infinitely often in p and below n; if there is none, the solutions have the form 0^{σ(0)}...(n-1)^{σ(n-1)}n^N.
statement.facts: tJ^n(id) ≡W g_n for every n > 0.

statement.name: Ginsburg–Sands theorem for CSC spaces
statement.definition: Every infinite CSC (countable second-countable, Dorais's formalization) space has an infinite subspace which is indiscrete, has the initial segment topology, has the final segment topology, is discrete, or has the cofinite topology.
statement.facts: GS is equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 4.6) and also equivalent to wGS. GS implies GScl, wGS and GST1.

statement.name: Weak and closure-enriched Ginsburg–Sands variants
statement.definition: wGS drops the discrete and cofinite alternatives in favour of 'T1'. GScl and wGScl are the restrictions of GS and wGS to CSC spaces for which the closure relation exists.
statement.facts: wGS is equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 4.6). wGScl is equivalent to CAC (Theorem 4.7). GScl is equivalent to GST1 (Theorem 4.8). The existence of the closure relation for every CSC space is equivalent to ACA0 (Proposition 4.3).

statement.name: Ginsburg–Sands theorem for T1 CSC spaces
statement.definition: Every infinite T1 CSC space has an infinite subspace which is discrete or has the cofinite topology.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, GST1 ↔ SGST1 + COH (Corollary 6.6), GST1 implies ADS (Theorem 6.5), and GST1 implies RT22 (Corollary 6.10). GST1 is strictly weaker than ACA0, since it has an ω-model without PA degrees and admits cone avoidance (Corollary 6.11). It has an ω-model consisting of low2 sets (Corollary 6.16). Every computable instance has a Δ⁰₂ discrete subspace or a computable cofinite subspace (Theorem 6.12). There is an ω-model of RT22 which is not a model of GST1 (Corollary 7.5). Whether it implies MTT22 or TT22 is open.

statement.name: Ginsburg–Sands theorem for stable T1 CSC spaces
statement.definition: The restriction of GST1 to stable CSC spaces, where a space is stable if for every x either {x} is open or every open set containing x is cofinite.
statement.facts: SGST1 + COH → GST1 (Proposition 6.4). SGST1 ↔ Σ02-Subset over RCA0 (Proposition 6.8). SGST1 implies SRT22 (Corollary 6.9).

statement.name: Σ⁰ₙ subset principle and Δ⁰ₙ subset principle
statement.definition: The scheme asserting that for every Σ⁰ₙ formula φ there is an infinite set Y equal to {x : φ(x)} or to its complement. The Δ⁰ₙ version requires φ and ψ to be Σ⁰ₙ with φ ↔ ψ.
statement.facts: Δ02-Subset is equivalent to D22 and SRT22, and Σ02-Subset is equivalent to SGST1 over RCA0. Σ02-Subset implies Δ02-Subset (hence SRT22). Every Σ⁰₂ set has an infinite low2 subset in it or its complement (Theorem 6.14). The proof of Theorem 7.1 shows there is an ω-model of RCA0 + RT22 (D22 + COH) not satisfying Σ02-Subset, and by relativization Δ0n-Subset does not imply Σ0n-Subset for n ≥ 2. Σ02-Subset does not imply Δ03-Subset. The hierarchy is summarized in Figure 2.

statement.notation: effectively discrete / effectively Hausdorff CSC space statements
statement.name: Effective discreteness statements for CSC spaces
statement.definition: Statements such as 'every discrete CSC space is effectively discrete' and 'every infinite effectively Hausdorff CSC space has an infinite effectively discrete subspace'.
statement.facts: The first is equivalent to ACA0 (Proposition 3.10). Every infinite Hausdorff CSC space has an infinite discrete subspace, provably in RCA0 (Theorem 5.2). The second statement is not provable in RCA0, since a computable counterexample exists (Theorem 5.4, Corollary 5.5); its exact strength is open (Question 8.1).

statement.name: Determinacy of win/lose games with Γ winning set (Nash equilibria of two-player games), Cantor space
statement.definition: Takes a two-player win/lose game on {0,1}^N whose winning set for player 1 is in Γ and returns a Nash equilibrium, i.e. a pair of strategies one of which is winning. Differs from catalogue det-sigma, which is on Baire space.
statement.facts: Det_A ≡W FindWS_A ≡W C_{0,1}^N for closed sets A (Theorem 9). Det_{D_{n+1}} ≡W C_{0,1}^N⋆lim^(n)-type degree: Det_{D_{n+1}} ≡W (C_{0,1}^N)^[n] (Theorem 15), and Det_D ≡W C_{0,1}^N ⋆ lim for D the differences of closed sets (introduction). Det_D is equivalent to the Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem by combining with [10]. Det_Γ ≡W Det of the complement class.

statement.name: Deciding the winner of Γ win/lose games
statement.definition: Same inputs as Det_Γ; decides which player (if any) has a winning strategy.
statement.facts: Win_A ≡W LPO (Proposition 10). Win_{D_{n+1}} ≡W LPO^[n] (Theorem 15). Win_{D(Γ)} ≤W LPO ⋆s Win^_Γ (Lemma 11).

statement.name: Finding winning strategies for Γ games (Cantor space)
statement.definition: Restriction of Det_Γ to games in which the first player has a winning strategy.
statement.facts: FindWS_A ≡W Det_A ≡W C_{0,1}^N (Theorem 9). FindWS_Γ ≡W its parallelization for pointclasses closed under a countable-union operation (Proposition 20).

statement.name: Nash equilibria of sequential games with finitely/countably many outcomes
statement.definition: Operations taking sequential games with countably many players and Γ-measurable outcome sets to Nash equilibria. NE^ap restricts to two players with antagonistic preferences.
statement.facts: NE^ap_Γ ≤W Det*_Γ × Win*_Γ (Theorem 21). NE_Γ ≤W Win^_Γ × Det^_Γ (Theorem 22). NE^ap_{O∪A} ≡W C_{0,1}^N × LPO* (Theorem 29). NE^ap_{D_{n+1}∪D_{n+1}} ≡W C_{0,1}^N^[n] × (LPO^[n])* (Theorem 30). C_{0,1}^N × LPO* ≤W NE_{O∪A} ≤W lim (Corollary 32).

statement.name: Subgame-perfect equilibria of antagonistic games
statement.definition: Takes a two-player game with finitely many outcomes and antagonistic preferences and returns a subgame-perfect equilibrium.
statement.facts: SPE_Γ ≤W Win^_Γ × Det^_Γ (Theorem 23). SPE_{O∪A} ≡W lim, and more generally SPE_{D_n∪D_n} ≡W lim^(n) (Theorem 31). Win^_{Γ1} ≤W SPE_Γ under the hypotheses of Lemma 28.

statement.name: Arithmetical levels of LLPO and LEM
statement.definition: Σ^0_n-LLPO takes a pair (p0,p1) of sequences and outputs i such that the Σ^0_n statement for p_i holds. Σ^0_n-LEM decides the truth of a Σ^0_n statement.
statement.facts: Σ^0_{n+1}-LLPO ≡W LLPO^[n] and Σ^0_{n+1}-LEM ≡W LPO^[n] (Proposition 13). Σ^0_n-LEM ≤W Win_{D_n} and the parallelization of Σ^0_n-LLPO ≤W Det_{D_n} (Lemma 14).

statement.name: Π¹₁ comprehension (as theory)
statement.definition: RCA₀ plus Π¹₁ comprehension. It is in the catalogue as pi11ca, but the paper uses it only as a base theory, not as a statement with ids in the extracted facts.
statement.facts: Over RCA₀, Π¹₁-CA₀ is equivalent to each of the following: every Π⁰₂ subspace of P(N) is homeomorphic to a UF space (Prop 3.17); every Π⁰₂ subspace of a UF space is itself a UF space (Cor 3.19); every UF space is homeomorphic to a second-countable Smyth-complete quasi-metric space (Thm 3.32); NP(P) is homeomorphic to some UF(P') for every countable P (Cor 3.18).

statement.notation: UF space / NP space / ideal space / Π⁰₂ subspace of P(N) / quasi-Polish space / countably presented frame
statement.name: Representations of quasi-Polish spaces
statement.definition: Formalizations in second-order arithmetic of second-countable T0 spaces: spaces of unbounded filters on a countable poset, of non-principal filters, of ideals, Π⁰₂ subspaces of P(N), second-countable Smyth-complete quasi-metric spaces, and sober spaces of countably presented frames. These are statements about spaces and their representations, not catalogue principles.
statement.facts: Over RCA₀ the following translations are provable: every quasi-Polish space is a UF space (Thm 3.23); every UF space is homeomorphic to a Π⁰₂ subspace of P(N) (Prop 3.11); NP spaces are equivalent to ideal spaces (Prop 3.9); NP spaces are equivalent to Π⁰₂ subspaces of P(N) (Prop 3.14); Π⁰₂ subspaces of P(N) are equivalent to countably presented frames with the congruence preorder (Prop 3.35, Cor 3.37). The converse translations Π⁰₂ subspace → UF space → quasi-Polish space each need Π¹₁-CA₀. Countably presented frames with the proof-theoretic relation ⊢ are shown spatial over ACA₀, and whether ACA₀ is needed is left open (Question 3.14).

statement.name: Existence of upward closures in posets
statement.definition: For every subset Q of a poset P, the upward closure of Q exists as a set.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA₀ over RCA₀.

items.loc: Corollary 3.20 proof, with Fact 2.4 and Proposition 2.5
items.quote: and so is the compact Σ11 -choice Σ11 -KCNN by Proposition 2.5.
items.argument: The proof of Proposition 2.5 shows Σ11-WKL ≡W Σ11-KC_NN, and the paper says Σ11-KC_NN is parallelizable. Parallelizability is invariant under Weihrauch equivalence, so Σ11-WKL is parallelizable. This also follows because Σ11-WKL ≡W the parallelization of Σ11-C_2 (Fact 2.4).
items.concerns: The paper states parallelizability for Σ11-KC_NN, not literally for Σ11-WKL.
reasons: deduction, not stated in the paper

statement.name: Σ11-choice principle on X (e.g. Σ11-C_N, Σ11-C_{N^N})
statement.definition: Given a code of a nonempty analytic subset of X, choose an element of it.
statement.facts: Σ11-C_{N^N} ≡W C_{N^N} (Proposition 2.2, with the reduction Σ11-C_{N^N} ≤W C_{N^N}). The parallelization of Σ11-C_2 is equivalent to Σ11-WKL and Π11-Sep. The parallelization of Σ11-C_N is equivalent to Σ11-KC, ATR2′ (arithmetically) and Π11-Tot2 (Corollary 2.9 and Theorem 2.10).

statement.name: Σ11 axiom of choice, restricted variants
statement.definition: Parallelization of Σ11-choice. The restrictions are fin, cof, foc, aof and aou (finite, cofinite, finite-or-cofinite, all-or-finite, all-or-unique), plus fosc (finite-or-strongly-cofinite).
statement.facts: Σ11-AC^fin ≡W Σ11-DC^fin <W Σ11-AC^aof ≡W Σ11-DC^aof ≡W Σ11-AC^aou ≡W Σ11-AC^fosc (Theorem 3.37, Corollaries 3.12 and 3.14). Σ11-AC^cof is Weihrauch incomparable with Σ11-AC^fin and Σ11-AC^aof (Corollary 3.23). Σ11-AC^aof and Σ11-AC^cof are not reducible to Σ11-KσC (Corollaries 3.19 and 3.26). Σ11-AC_{N^N} <W Σ11-DC_{N^N} (Theorem 3.34). Upward density of the Medvedev lattices of Σ11-AC^cof, Σ11-AC^foc and Σ11-AC_{N^N} (Theorems 3.24, 3.27, 3.29).

statement.name: Σ11 dependent choice
statement.definition: Given a Σ11 set Y and a Σ11 relation satisfying the premise of dependent choice, return a sequence f with f(0) = a0 and R(f(n), f(n+1)) for all n.
statement.facts: C_{N^N} ≡W [Σ11-DC_{N^N}]mv ≡W [Σ11-DC_N]mv (Proposition 2.2). Σ11-DC_{N^N} ≡W Σ11-AC^fin ⋆ Σ11-AC^cof (Theorem 3.34). Σ11-AC ⋆ Σ11-AC ≡W Σ11-AC ⋆ Σ11-AC ⋆ Σ11-AC, so compositional powers stabilize at level two.

statement.name: Compact and σ-compact Σ11 choice
statement.definition: Σ11-choice restricted to compact Σ11 sets. The σ-compact version takes a sequence of compact Σ11 sets, at least one nonempty.
statement.facts: Σ11-KC ≡W Σ11-WKL ≡W the parallelization of Σ11-C_2 (Proposition 2.5, Fact 2.4). Σ11-KσC is not parallelizable, and Σ11-KC <W Σ11-KσC (Corollary 3.20).

statement.name: Totalization and diagonalization for partial Π11 functions
statement.definition: Given a partial Π11 function into 2 (or ω), find a total extension. DNC: given a sequence of partial Π11 functions, find a total function diagonalizing against it.
statement.facts: The parallelization of Σ11-C_2 ≡W Π11-Tot2 ≡W Π11-DNC2 (Proposition 2.6). The parallelization of Σ11-C^aou_N ≡W Π11-TotN (Proposition 2.7). Π11-DNCN ≤W Π11-DNC2 ≤W Π11-TotN.

statement.name: Variants of two-sided ATR
statement.definition: ATR2′: given a linear order, return a jump hierarchy on a large initial segment (one containing the well-founded part) or an infinite descending sequence. ATR2^po: the same as ATR2 for partial orders.
statement.facts: The parallelization of ATR2′ is arithmetically Weihrauch equivalent to Σ11-KC and to the parallelization of Σ11-C^aou_N (Theorem 2.10). Σ11-C^aou_N ≤W ATR2^po (Proposition 2.13). ATR ≤W ATR2′ ≤W ATR2 ≤W ATR2^po ≤W Σ11-C_{N^N}. Whether ATR2, ATR2′ and ATR2^po are arithmetically equivalent is open (Question 2.14).

statement.name: Totalization of Σ11 unique choice
statement.definition: Σ11-choice restricted to singletons, extended to a total problem: any value is accepted if the set is not a singleton.
statement.facts: Σ11-UC^tot_X ≡W Σ11-C^aou_X for X a Δ11 subset of N (Proposition 2.8). The parallelization of Σ11-UC^tot_2 ≡W Σ11-KC_{N^N} (Corollary 2.9).

statement.name: Cousin's lemma for Baire 2 (Baire n) functions
statement.definition: Every Baire n gauge δ : [0,1] → R+ has a δ-fine partition. Baire n+1 functions are pointwise Cauchy sequences of Baire n functions, and Baire 0 functions are the total continuous functions.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, CL_Bn implies WKL0 for every n (Theorem 7.1.6). CL_B2 implies ATR0 (Theorem 7.4.1), and implies ACA0+ (remark after Theorem 7.3.2). ACA0 does not imply CL_B2 (Theorem 7.3.2). For n ≥ 2, CL_Bn is provable in Π11-CA0 and implies ATR0 (Theorem 8.1(iii)). CL_B(n+1) implies CL_Bn since the Baire classes are nested. The strength of CL_B1 beyond implying ACA0 is open (Question 8.2).

statement.name: Sequential completeness of the reals (every Cauchy sequence in [0,1] has a limit)
statement.definition: Every Cauchy sequence of real numbers in [0,1] has a limit.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, CL_B1 implies SC (Theorem 7.2.2). SC is equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (cited from Friedman 1976).

items.loc: Section 2.3, paragraph after Theorem 2.21's preceding text (WKL0 vs ACA0)
items.quote: which is strictly stronger than RCA0 , and strictly weaker than ACA0 .
items.concerns: Standard fact, stated in passing (also 'ACA0 implies WKL0' in Section 5.1).

statement.name: Every Artinian ring is Noetherian
statement.definition: If R is a commutative ring with identity in which every decreasing chain of ideals stabilizes, then every increasing chain of ideals stabilizes.
statement.facts: Over RCA0 it implies WKL0 and is implied by ACA0 (Theorem 1.12).

statement.name: Every Artinian ring is strongly Noetherian (finite length)
statement.definition: Every Artinian ring has finite length, i.e. there is a bound on the length of strictly increasing chains of ideals.
statement.facts: Provable in ACA0 (Theorem 5.1); over RCA0+BΣ2 it is equivalent to ACA0 (Theorem 1.13).

statement.name: Properties of Artinian rings (integral domains are fields, primes are maximal, Jacobson radical equals nilradical, J is t-nilpotent, R/N is Noetherian)
statement.definition: 2: Artinian integral domains are fields. 3: in an Artinian ring every prime ideal is maximal. 4: in an Artinian ring J and N exist and are equal. 5: if R is Artinian and J exists then J is t-nilpotent. 6: if R is Artinian and N exists then R/N is Noetherian.
statement.facts: Over RCA0+IΣ2 each is equivalent to WKL0; the reversals 2-6 imply WKL0 over RCA0 (Section 4.4).

statement.notation: Every ring that is not a field contains a nontrivial ideal
statement.name: Nontrivial ideals in non-fields
statement.definition: Every ring that is not a field contains a nontrivial ideal.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (cited).

statement.notation: Every vector space of dimension greater than 1 contains a nontrivial proper subspace
statement.name: Nontrivial proper subspaces
statement.definition: Every vector space of dimension greater than 1 contains a nontrivial proper subspace.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (cited).

statement.name: Bolzano–Weierstrass for countable sets (injection-countable) / enumerability of countable sets
statement.definition: Higher-order statements: every countable set A ⊂ 2^N (injection to N) has a supremum (BWC_0), equivalently can be enumerated by a sequence (cocode_0). Variants with sequence, functionals, pointwise ordering.
statement.facts: Theorem 2.11 (over ACA_0^ω): cocode_0 ↔ [BWC_0 + IND_0] ↔ range_0 ↔ BWC_0^pwo; Theorem 2.30: cocode_0 ↔ BWC_0^pwo ↔ accu ↔ accu' ↔ ccc; Theorems 2.33, 2.34, 2.35: equivalent to [CWO^ω + IND_0], [cloq + IND_0], [cloq' + IND_0]; Theorem 3.3: ↔ LIN_0 ↔ HBC_0^seq; Theorem 3.7: Σ-SEP implies cocode_0; Corollary 3.8: Σ-SEP_C^- ↔ cocode_0; Theorems 3.34/3.35: equivalent to the Jordan decomposition theorem (given IND_2 + CUC_fin) and to enumerating discontinuities of BV/regulated functions; Theorem 3.19: CUC → cocode_0 → CUC(2) → cocode_1; Theorem 3.43: unordered sums.

statement.name: Bolzano–Weierstrass for strongly countable sets (bijection to N) / enumerability of strongly countable sets
statement.definition: Higher-order statements: every strongly countable set A ⊂ 2^N (bijection to N) has a supremum (BWC_1), equivalently can be enumerated (cocode_1).
statement.facts: Theorem 2.5: [BWC_1 + IND_1] ↔ BWC_1^pwo ↔ cocode_1; Theorem 2.7: cocode_1 ↔ Δ-CA_C^- ↔ enumerating subsets of strongly countable sets; Corollary 2.6: relation to hyperarithmetical analysis; Theorem 2.16: Z_2^ω + CBN + IND_0 cannot prove NBI, so CBN does not imply cocode_1; Theorem 3.14/Corollary 3.15: Π-SEP implies cocode_1, Π-SEP! ↔ cocode_1; Corollary 3.20: cocode_1 ↔ CUC_1(2); Corollary 3.44.

statement.name: Cantor–Bernstein theorem for N
statement.definition: A countable set A ⊂ R (injection to N) is strongly countable if there is a sequence of pairwise distinct reals in A.
statement.facts: [CBN + cocode_1] ↔ cocode_0; independent of BWC_1 (Theorem 2.16); Π^1_1-CA_0^ω + CBN proves Π^1_2-CA_0 (Theorem 2.18); ACA_0^ω proves BOOT_C^- ↔ CBN^+ (Corollary 2.19); ccc_1 ↔ CBN ↔ accu_1 (Corollary 2.32).

statement.name: Uncountable Heine–Borel (Cousin) / Heine–Borel with ψ / projection axiom / higher-order Σ^0_1 separation
statement.definition: Higher-order versions: HBU finite subcover of canonical covering by Ψ:R→R+; HBT for ψ:[0,1]→R; BOOT is projection axiom; Σ-SEP is separation for Σ-formulas with type-2 parameters.
statement.facts: BOOT → HBT → BWC_0 → BWC_1 (assuming fragment of induction); BOOT → Σ-SEP → BWC_0 → BWC_1; Theorem 3.10: HBU ↔ Σ-SEP over ACA_0^ω + A_0 (with bounded-Σ-SEP); Corollary 3.11 HBT + bounded-Σ-SEP ↔ Σ-SEP.

statement.name: Jordan decomposition theorem for BV functions
statement.definition: A BV function f:[0,1]→R is the difference of two non-decreasing functions, in the higher-order setting.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.34: over ACA_0^ω + IND_2 + CUC_fin equivalent to cocode_0 and to enumerating discontinuities of BV functions; Remark 3.28: does not imply (∃^2).

statement.name: Countable union theorem variants
statement.definition: CUC: countable union of enumerable sets of reals is enumerable; CUC(2) for two-element sets; RUC: R is not a countable union of enumerable sets; NFσ: some set of reals is not Fσ; CUC_fin finite-set fragment.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.19: CUC → cocode_0 → CUC(2) → cocode_1 and NFσ → RUC → NIN; Corollary 3.20: cocode_0 ↔ CUC_0(2), cocode_1 ↔ CUC_1(2); Corollary 3.22: [cloq'_seq + IND_0] ↔ CUC; Corollary 3.23: Z_2^Ω + QF-AC proves CUC; Z_2^ω + QF-AC cannot prove RUC.

statement.name: No injection / no bijection from [0,1] to N
statement.definition: There is no injection (resp. bijection) from [0,1] to N.
statement.facts: Principle 2.20 implies NIN (Theorem 2.25); cocode_1 → NBI; Z_2^ω + CBN + IND_0 cannot prove NBI.

statement.notation: accu, accu', ccc, cloq, cloq', CWO^ω
statement.name: Limit-point, countable chain condition, and countable linear order principles going back to Cantor
statement.definition: accu: non-enumerable closed set in R has a limit point; ccc: disjoint open intervals family is enumerable; cloq/cloq': countable linear orders embed into Q / countable dense orders without endpoints isomorphic to Q; CWO^ω: comparability of countable well-orders.
statement.facts: Equivalent to cocode_0 together with IND_0 where needed (Theorems 2.30, 2.33, 2.34, Corollary 2.35); Corollary 2.27: Π^1_1-CA_0^ω cannot prove PST or CBT.

statement.notation: Analytic-Regularity (all analytic sets A ⊂ [0,1] are Lebesgue-regular)
statement.name: Lebesgue-regularity of analytic sets
statement.definition: Every analytic set A ⊂ [0,1] has equal outer and inner Lebesgue measure, where outer measure is the infimum of λ(B) over open B ⊇ A and inner measure is the supremum of λ(B) over compact B ⊆ A.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Σ¹₁-Induction over ATR₀ (Theorem 1); the reversal is Lemma 6 over ACA₀. Σ¹₁-IND with ATR₀ also gives regularity of all analytic sets A ⊂ R (Theorem 33).

statement.notation: Analytic-Measurability (all analytic sets A ⊂ [0,1] are Lebesgue-measurable)
statement.name: Lebesgue-measurability of analytic sets
statement.definition: Every analytic set A ⊂ [0,1] is Lebesgue-regular and the common value λ(A) exists as a real number.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Π¹₁-CA₀ over ATR₀ (Theorem 2); the reversal is Lemma 7 over ACA₀. Π¹₁-CA₀ gives measurability of all analytic A ⊂ R (Theorem 34).

statement.name: Σ¹₁-Induction
statement.definition: The induction scheme for Σ¹₁ formulas (with set parameters), for natural numbers.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA₀ to finite Σ¹₁-Comprehension (Lemma 5). Equivalent to regularity of analytic sets over ATR₀ (Theorem 1). Nemoto's result, cited in the introduction, gives equivalence over ATR₀ with determinacy of games with payoff in B(Δ⁰₁, Σ⁰₂).

statement.name: Finite Σ¹₁ comprehension
statement.definition: For every Σ¹₁ formula φ and every n there is a set X ⊆ N with ∀m ≤ n (m ∈ X ↔ φ(m)).
statement.facts: Equivalent to Σ¹₁-Induction over RCA₀ (Lemma 5).

statement.name: Special fan functionals
statement.definition: Type-3 functionals Θ that, for every G^2, output a finite sequence of binary sequences g such that the neighbourhoods [gG(g)] cover Cantor space.
statement.facts: Computable from the intuitionistic fan functional (Theorem 3.4). Not computable in ∃2 or any type-two functional (Theorem 3.7, Corollary 3.8). Computable from ∃3 (Theorem 3.9). RCA0^ω + (∃Θ)SFF(Θ) is conservative over RCA0 + WKL (Corollary 3.5). Θ with ∃2 computes a realiser for ATR0 (Corollary 6.6). κ computes Θ, but not vice versa (Theorem 6.17).

statement.name: Weak fan functionals
statement.definition: Type-3 functionals Λ(G,k) outputting a finite list of binary sequences whose neighbourhoods [gG(g)] have measure at least 1-2^{-k}.
statement.facts: Not computable in ∃2 (Theorem 3.13). There is a Λ such that no Θ is computable in Λ and ∃2 (Theorem 3.14). RCA0^ω + (∃Λ)WCF(Λ) is conservative over RCA0 + WWKL (Theorem 3.15). There is a Λ0 giving hyperarithmetical output on hyperarithmetical input (Section 5.4).

statement.name: Nonstandard compactness of Cantor space
statement.definition: (∀α≤1)(∃st β≤1)(α≈β): every binary sequence is infinitely close to a standard binary sequence; the nonstandard counterpart of WKL.
statement.facts: Equivalent in P0 to normal forms (4.8) and (N) involving special fan functionals (Theorem 4.3). P0+STP is conservative over RCA0^2+WKL (Corollary 4.4). Not provable from P+Π01-TRANS (Theorem 4.5), nor from P+Π11-TRANS (Corollary 4.6). Not provable from P0+LMP (Theorem 4.11) nor from P+Π01-TRANS+LMP (Theorem 4.12). P0+Π01-TRANS+STP proves ATR0^st (Theorem 6.4). P proves STP ↔ CCns (Theorem 6.18).

statement.name: Nonstandard counterpart of WWKL
statement.definition: For every binary tree T with µ(T) ≫ 0 there is a standard β≤1 with βm ∈ T for all standard m.
statement.facts: Equivalent in P0 to normal forms involving weak fan functionals (Theorem 4.9). P+Π11-TRANS does not prove LMP (Theorem 4.10). P0+Π01-TRANS+LMP does not prove ATR0^st (Theorem 6.3).

statement.name: Transfer limited to Π01 resp. Π11 formulas
statement.definition: Fragments of the Transfer axiom of Nelson's IST, the nonstandard counterparts of ACA0 and Π11-CA0.
statement.facts: P+Π01-TRANS does not prove ATR0^st (Theorem 6.2). P0+Π01-TRANS proves Δ11-CA^st (Theorem 6.1).

statement.name: Higher-order functionals
statement.definition: Intuitionistic and classical fan functionals, comprehension functionals, the Suslin functional, and the choice-like functional κ.
statement.facts: RCA0^ω + (∃Ω)MUC(Ω) is conservative over RCA0 + WKL (Theorem 3.2). Borel's Θ computes the Suslin functional (Corollary 5.8). RCA0^ω+(∃Θ)SFF(Θ) proves (µ2) ↔ UATR, while RCA0^ω+WKL does not (Corollary 6.12).

statement.name: First-order (recursive) version of RT^2_2
statement.definition: For any X and c : [N]^2 → 2, if IΣ^X_1 fails, then there is an index of a Δ^X_1 set which is infinite and homogeneous for c.
statement.facts: RCA0* + RT^2_2 proves it. Over RCA0* + ¬IΣ^0_1 it is equivalent to RT^2_2, so RT^2_2 is equivalent to a Π^1_1 statement there. It is not provable in RCA0*, even in its lightface version.

statement.name: First-jump control statement for RT^2_2
statement.definition: For any sets X, Z with X′ ≪ Z′ and any coloring c : [N]^2 → 2 with c ≤_T X, there is an index of a Σ^Z_2 set H which is infinite homogeneous for c and satisfies (X ⊕ H)′ ≪ Z′.
statement.facts: RCA0 + IΣ^0_2 proves it (Theorem 5). RCA0 + RT^2_2 proves it (Theorem 14). Whether RCA0 + BΣ^0_2 proves it is open; RT^2_2 is Π^1_1-conservative over RCA0 + BΣ^0_2 if and only if RCA0 + BΣ^0_2 proves it (Corollary 7). It can be formulated as a Π^0_5 statement.

statement.name: Bounded enumeration scheme
statement.definition: A scheme of sentences from Chong–Slaman–Yang [7], now known to be equivalent to the well-orderedness of ω, ω^ω, ….
statement.facts: RCA0 + RT^2_2 + BME is a Π^0_4-conservative extension of RCA0 + BΣ^0_2 + BME (Theorem 10).

items.quote: RT22 is Π11 -conservative over RCA0 together with the Σ02 -induction
reasons: attributed by the paper to Cholak, Jockusch and Slaman [1]: cite the original

items.quote: Since Q<ω is a subset of Q̃ it is obvious that NWT implies GHT even in RCA0 .

verifier.reason: The argument uses Q^{<ω} ⊆ Q̃, which relies on the paper's NWT covering sequences of all countable lengths. The catalogue's NWT is stated for S_α(Q) with α fixed. If S_α means sequences of length exactly α, finite sequences of all lengths are not contained in any single S_α. A human should check the catalogue's intended meaning of S_α(Q) and whether it coincides with the paper's Q̃.

items.quote: RCA0 proves that NWT implies ATR0 .
items.concerns: Deduced from Shore's theorem that wqo of countable well-orderings implies ATR0.

verifier.reason: Corollary 5.2 uses the paper's NWT for the full class Q̃ with a one-element Q, which gives that all countable well-orderings are wqo, and then applies Shore's theorem. The catalogue states NWT for S_α(Q) with α fixed. With α fixed and Q a singleton, S_α(Q) is either a single element (length exactly α) or the well-orders below α, not the class of all countable well-orderings. A human should check that the catalogue's nwt is meant to be Marcone's Q̃ version, or that the per-α form still implies ATR₀.

statement.name: Locally minimal bad array lemma
statement.definition: For a quasi-order (Q,≼), a well-founded relation <′ compatible with ≼ and a bad Q-array f, there is a g ≤′ f which is locally minimal bad with respect to <′.
statement.facts: Provable in Π11-CA0 (Theorem 2.17). Equivalent over RCA0 to Π11-CA0 (Theorem 6.5), hence not provable in ATR0.

statement.name: Minimal bad sequence lemma
statement.definition: For a quasi-order Q and a well-founded relation <′ compatible with it, if a bad Q-sequence exists then a Q-sequence that is minimal bad with respect to <′ exists.
statement.facts: Implies ACA0 over RCA0 (Lemma 6.3). Equivalent over RCA0 to Π11-CA0 and to the locally minimal bad array lemma (Theorem 6.5).

statement.name: Existence of leftmost paths through non-well-founded trees
statement.definition: If T is a non-well-founded tree then there is a leftmost path through T.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to Π11-CA0 and to the minimal bad sequence lemma (Theorem 6.5).

statement.notation: bqo statements (Q bqo, Q̃ bqo, countable bqo)
statement.name: Better-quasi-ordering
statement.definition: A countable quasi-order is bqo if every Q-array indexed by a barrier is good. The paper also uses a hereditarily indecomposable class H and B-wqo.
statement.facts: Lemma 4.2 (ATR0): if Q<ω is a countable bqo then H is bqo. Theorem 5.5: over ATR0, GHT and NWT are equivalent. Shore's theorem (cited, Theorem 5.1): over RCA0, the statement that the class of countable well-orderings is wqo under embeddability implies ATR0.

items.quote: Theorem 3.10. RCA0 + SRT22 0 2-RWKL.

statement.name: Ramsey-type König's lemma
statement.definition: For every infinite finitely branching subtree of N^{<N}, there is an infinite homogeneous partial function.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3.17). Also equivalent to ACA0 when restricted to trees with at most two successors per node.

statement.name: Ramsey-type bounded König's lemma
statement.definition: Ramsey-type König's lemma for infinite bounded subtrees of N^{<N}.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL over RCA0 (Theorem 3.19). Also WKL for trees bounded by an arbitrarily slow order function.

statement.name: Localized Ramsey-type weak König's lemma
statement.definition: For every infinite tree T ⊆ 2^{<N} and infinite X, there is an infinite H ⊆ X homogeneous for T.
statement.facts: Equivalent to RWKL over RCA0 (Lemma 3.22).

statement.name: Localized Ramsey-type weak weak König's lemma
statement.definition: RWWKL for trees of positive measure, with the homogeneous set required to be a subset of a given infinite X.
statement.facts: Equivalent to DNR and RWWKL over RCA0 (Theorem 3.24).

statement.name: Ramsey-type WKL for k-branching trees
statement.definition: RWKL (resp. LRWKL) for infinite subtrees of k^{<N}.
statement.facts: For fixed k ≥ 2 each is equivalent to RWKL over RCA0 (Theorem 3.27). ∀k RWKL_k implies RT^1 (equivalently BΣ02) over RCA0. WKL0 does not prove ∀k RWKL_k, but WKL0 + BΣ02 does.

statement.name: Localized and r.e. variants of Ramsey-type satisfiability
statement.loc: Definition 4.3 and the paragraph after it
statement.definition: Localized (infinite H ⊆ X) and r.e. (list of formulas) variants of RSAT.
statement.facts: All equivalent to RWKL and RSAT over RCA0 (Theorem 4.7).

statement.name: Localized Ramsey-type graph k-coloring
statement.definition: RCOLOR_k with the infinite homogeneous set required to be a subset of a given infinite X ⊆ V.
statement.facts: Equivalent to RWKL for k ≥ 3 (Corollary 5.14). Equivalent to RCOLOR_2 for k = 2 (Theorem 5.17).

statement.name: Ramsey-type graph k-coloring for k ≥ 4
statement.definition: For every infinite locally k-colorable graph there is an infinite k-homogeneous set.
statement.facts: Equivalent to RWKL for every standard k ≥ 3 (Corollary 5.14). Only k = 3 and k = 2 are in the catalogue.

statement.name: Packed Ramsey-type weak König's lemma
statement.definition: For every order function g with g(n) ≤ n and every infinite T ⊆ 2^{<N}, there is an infinite h homogeneous for T and packed for g.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL over RCA0.

statement.name: Homogeneous sets for color 0 for trees with no eventually-1 path
statement.definition: For every infinite tree T ⊆ 2^{<N} with no path eventually 1, there is an infinite set homogeneous for T with color 0.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL over RCA0.

statement.name: Higher relativized RWWKL and DNR
statement.definition: RWWKL for X^{(n-1)}-computable trees of positive measure, and DNR relative to X^{(n-1)}.
statement.facts: n-RWWKL → n-DNR over RCA0 + BΣ0n (Lemma 3.6). n-DNR → n-RWWKL over RCA0 + IΣ0n (Lemma 3.7). They are equivalent over RCA0 + IΣ0n (Theorem 3.8). Whether 2-RWWKL implies BΣ02 is open (Question 3.9). The n = 2 case lies in the catalogue as rwwkl2 and dnr0, but only over bases not expressible as a reduction id.

statement.name: Artinian rings are Noetherian
statement.definition: Every Artinian ring (commutative with identity) is Noetherian.
statement.facts: WKL0 proves ART0 over RCA0 (Theorem 8.3), hence ART0 is equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (Corollary 8.4, using [Con10, Theorem 4.1]). WKL0 + IΣ2 proves ART0 (Theorem 5.2, two proofs). ART0 implies WKL0 over RCA0 + IΣ2 (Section 5 intro, from [Con10]).

statement.name: Local Artinian rings are Noetherian
statement.definition: Every local Artinian ring is Noetherian.
statement.facts: WKL0 + BΣ2 proves ARTl0 (Lemma 8.1). WKL0 proves ARTl0 (Lemma 8.2). WKL0 + IΣ2 proves it as a consequence of Theorem 5.2.

statement.name: Structure theorem for Artinian rings
statement.definition: Every Artinian ring is a finite direct product of local Artinian rings.
statement.facts: WKL0 implies ARTs0 over RCA0 (Theorem 5.5). ARTs0 implies WKL0 over RCA0 (Theorem 6.2). Hence ARTs0 is equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Nilpotence of the Jacobson radical of an Artinian ring
statement.definition: The Jacobson radical of an Artinian ring exists and is nilpotent.
statement.facts: WKL0 implies NIL0 over RCA0 (Theorem 5.1). NIL0 implies WKL0 over RCA0 (Theorem 6.1). Hence NIL0 is equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Chinese Remainder Theorem
statement.definition: If A1,...,An are ideals of a commutative ring R with Ai + Aj = R for i<j, then R → R/A1 × ... × R/An is surjective with kernel A1···An = A1 ∩ ... ∩ An.
statement.facts: RCA0 proves CRT0, without any extra induction (Lemma 5.4).

statement.name: Turing jump functional (type-two comprehension)
statement.definition: There is a functional ϕ² ≤ 1 deciding (∃n)(f(n)=0) for every f¹; over RCA₀^ω it yields ACA₀ (conservatively).
statement.facts: Used in disjunctions such as (∃²) ↔ [FF + ¬MUC], WKL ↔ [(∃²) ∨ HBU_c], (∃³) ↔ [(κ₀³) + (∃²)], (∃²) ↔ [UATR ∨ ¬HBU].

statement.name: Suslin functional
statement.definition: A functional S² ≤ 1 deciding Σ¹₁-formulas; yields Π¹₁-CA₀.
statement.facts: MUC ↔ [(κ₀³)+WKL+¬(S²)] (Theorem 3.3); MUC ↔ [FF+(Z³)+¬(S²)] (Corollary 3.4).

statement.name: Full second-order comprehension functional
statement.definition: There is E³ ≤ 1 deciding (∃f¹)Y(f)=0 for every Y²; Z₂^Ω = RCA₀^ω + (∃³).
statement.facts: (∃³) ↔ [(κ₀³)+(∃²)] and (∃³) ↔ [(Z³)+(∃²)] (Corollary 3.2), (∃³) ↔ [FF+(Z³)+¬MUC] (Theorem 3.7); MUC ↔ [(κ₀³)+WKL+¬(∃³)].

statement.name: Intuitionistic fan functional
statement.definition: There is Ω³ giving a modulus of uniform continuity on Cantor space for every Y².
statement.facts: Theorem 3.3: MUC ↔ [(κ₀³)+WKL+¬(∃²)] over RCA₀^ω+QF-AC^{2,0}; Corollary 3.4: MUC ↔ [FF+¬(∃²)]; FF ↔ [(∃²)∨MUC] over RCA₀^ω (Theorem 3.6); (κ₀³)+WKL ↔ (∃³)∨MUC.

statement.name: Classical fan functional
statement.definition: There is Φ³ giving a modulus of uniform continuity on Cantor space for every continuous Y².
statement.facts: (∃²)→FF→WKL; FF ↔ [(∃²)∨MUC]; FF ↔ [(∃²)∨(κ₀³)] over WKL₀^ω+QF-AC^{2,0}; (κ₀³) ↔ (Z³)+FF (Theorem 3.1).

statement.name: Comprehension functional for Cantor space
statement.definition: There is κ₀³ deciding (∃f∈C)(Y(f)>0) for each Y².
statement.facts: Splits as (Z³)+FF over WKL₀^ω+QF-AC^{2,0} (Theorem 3.1); (κ₀³)+WKL ↔ (Z³)+FF (Corollary 3.2); (∃³) ↔ [(κ₀³)+(∃²)]; Theorem 3.5: if MUC→W and (∃³)→W→(κ₀³) then W ↔ (κ₀³).

statement.name: Continuity-testing functional on Baire space
statement.definition: There is Z³ deciding whether Y² is continuous on Baire space.
statement.facts: (Z³) ↔ [(∃³)∨¬(∃²)] ↔ [(∃³)∨¬FF∨MUC] (Theorem 3.7); (∃³) ↔ (∃²)+(Z³) over RCA₀^ω.

statement.name: Uncountable Heine-Borel compactness (Cousin's lemma)
statement.definition: For every Ψ:R→R⁺ there are finitely many points y₁..y_k whose intervals I_{y_i}^Ψ cover [0,1].
statement.facts: WKL ↔ [X ∨ HBU] for ACA₀→X→WKL₀ (Theorem 3.8); (∃²) ↔ [UATR ∨ ¬HBU] (Theorem 3.15, Corollary 3.19); LIN ↔ [HBU ∨ ¬WKL]; MUC→HBU; ZΩ₂ proves HBU, Z₂^ω does not; WKL₀^ω+HBU conservative over WKL₀.

statement.name: Heine-Borel compactness for Cantor space
statement.definition: For every G² there are f₁..f_k with the basic sets [f_i G(f_i)] covering Cantor space; equivalent to HBU.
statement.facts: WKL ↔ [(∃²)∨HBU_c] ↔ [FF∨HBU_c] (Theorem 3.8); HBU_c→WKL.

statement.name: Trivially uniform ATR₀
statement.definition: There is Φ giving the hierarchy for every well-ordering X and arithmetical operator coded by f.
statement.facts: (∃²) ↔ [UATR ∨ ¬HBU] over RCA₀^ω+FF+QF-AC^{2,1}; also (∃²) ↔ [UATR ∨ ¬LIN] over RCA₀^ω+QF-AC^{2,1}.

statement.name: Lindelöf lemma (higher-order)
statement.definition: For every Ψ:R→R⁺ there is a sequence of open intervals covering R, each of the form I_x^Ψ.
statement.facts: LIN ↔ [HBU ∨ ¬WKL] ↔ [HBU ∨ ¬X] (Theorem 3.18); [LIN+WKL] ↔ HBU; ¬LIN ↔ [WKL+¬HBU] and ¬LIN→(∃²); LIN ↔ [WHBU ∨ ¬WWKL].

statement.name: Weak Heine-Borel compactness
statement.definition: For every Ψ:R→R⁺ and k there are y₁..y_n with Σ|I_{y_i}^Ψ| ≥ 1−2^{-k}.
statement.facts: WWKL ↔ [(∃²)∨WHBU] ↔ [X∨WHBU] (Theorem 3.20); WWKL ↔ [Π¹₁-CA₀∨(∃²)∨WHBU]; WHBU∨Σ⁰₂-IND ↔ WWKL∨Σ⁰₂-IND; WHBU is not provable in Π¹_k-CA₀^ω for any k.

statement.name: Periodic points theorem of Friedman-Simpson-Yu
statement.definition: For all k and compact metric spaces X and continuous F:X→X, F^k is continuous; equivalent over RCA₀ to WKL ∨ Σ⁰₂-IND.
statement.facts: T₁ ↔ [HBU∨Σ⁰₂-IND] ↔ [WKL∨Σ⁰₂-IND] ↔ [FF∨HBU∨Σ⁰₂-IND]; T₁ ↔ (T₀∨Σ⁰₂-IND); (T₀∨T₁) ↔ T₁.

statement.name: Contraposition of Belanger's theorem (model theory)
statement.definition: Negation of: there is a complete theory with a non-principal type and only finitely many models up to isomorphism; T₀ ↔ WKL₀ + ¬ACA₀.
statement.facts: T₀ ↔ [WKL₀+¬ACA₀] ↔ [HBU+¬ACA₀] over RCA₀^ω; WKL₀ ↔ [ACA₀∨T₀]; RCA₀^ω+T₀ proves HBU.

statement.name: n-weak weak König's lemma
statement.definition: WWKL for trees computable in the n-th Turing jump, as in Avigad–Dean–Rute.
statement.facts: For n≥1, [HBU ∨ n-WWKL] ↔ [WKL ∨ n-WWKL] over RCA₀^ω.

statement.name: Sequential version of a principle (ω parallel applications)
statement.definition: Instances are sequences of instances of P and solutions are sequences of solutions. It is the parallelization of P.
statement.facts: Squashing Theorem: for total P with finite tolerance, P^2 ≤sW P implies SeqP ≤sW P. SeqWKL ≡sW WKL, WKL ≤sW SeqWWKL, SeqWWKL ≰W WWKL. Sequential forms of RT^n_k and TS^n_k can code ∅^(n).

statement.name: WWKL with measure bound q
statement.definition: Every subtree T of 2^{<ω} with |{σ ∈ 2^n : σ ∈ T}|/2^n ≥ q for all n has an infinite path.
statement.facts: RCA0 proves WWKL ↔ q-WWKL for each q (Proposition 4.4 formalized). Proposition 4.7: p-WWKL ≰W q-WWKL for rationals p<q<1. There is no effective procedure uniformly blowing up the measure and also yielding uniform reductions (Proposition 4.5).

statement.name: Thin set theorem for n-tuples and k colors
statement.definition: Every f: [N]^n → k (k ∈ {2,3,...,ω}) has an infinite thin set; the solution includes the omitted color.
statement.facts: TS^n_2 is RT^n_2. Implications go in the opposite direction to RT: TS^n_k ≤sW TS^n_j for j<k. TS^{n+2}_{2^n} implies ACA over RCA0. TS^3_8 + CAC, TS^3_7 + ADS and TS^3_6 + SHER each imply RT^2_2 over RCA0, and TS^3_3 implies RT^2_{<∞}. For every n, SeqTS^n_k has a computable instance with no ∅^(n)-computable solution but every solution computes ∅^(n). Theorem 5.27: TS^1_j ≰W TS^1_k for j<k; Theorem 5.28 (Hirschfeldt–Jockusch) extends this to n>1. Only some instances (ts23, ts24, ts2, ts13) are in the catalogue.

statement.name: Thin set theorem for singletons with infinitely many colors
statement.definition: Every f: N → ω has an infinite thin set (omitting a color).
statement.facts: Every computable instance of SeqTS^1_ω has a ∅'-computable solution (Proposition 5.22), SeqTS^1_ω ≤sW TJ^1, and every computable instance has a low2 solution (Theorem 5.24). SeqTS^1_ω ≤sW L2 (Corollary 5.26). Also a cone-avoidance statement is mentioned.

statement.name: Semi-trivial Ramsey principle
statement.definition: Every semi-trivial coloring f: [N]^2 → 2 has an infinite homogeneous set.
statement.facts: Equivalent to RT^1_{<∞} over RCA0 but apparently not strongly Weihrauch equivalent. CAC, ADS and SHER each imply it and none of these implications reverse.

statement.name: Chain–antichain principle as semi-transitive colorings
statement.definition: Every semi-transitive coloring f: [N]^2 → 2 has an infinite homogeneous set.
statement.facts: Studied by Hirschfeldt and Shore: CAC implies ADS over RCA0 and is strictly weaker than RT^2_2. Used in RCA0 ⊢ (TS^3_8 + CAC) → RT^2_2.

statement.name: Rainbow Ramsey theorem (general exponent and bound)
statement.definition: Every k-bounded f: [ω]^n → ω has an infinite rainbow; RRT^n_{<∞} is (∀k) RRT^n_k.
statement.facts: Every computable instance of SeqRRT^1_{<∞} has a computable solution. Every computable instance of SeqRRT^2_k has a solution computable in any 2-random (Theorem 6.6). SeqRRT^2_{<∞} ≰W 2-WWKL (Corollary 6.12), and some computable instance has no solution computable from some 2-random (Proposition 6.11).

statement.name: n-th iterated Turing jump
statement.definition: Multi-valued function sending X to X^(n).
statement.facts: TJ^n ≤sW SeqRT^n_2. SeqTS^n_k ≰W TJ^n for all n ≥ 1, k ≥ 2. Only n=1 is in the catalogue (tj).

statement.name: WKL for trees with bounded prefix-free subsets
statement.definition: An infinite binary tree T ⊆ 2^{<N} has a path if there is c such that every prefix-free P ⊆ T has |P| ≤ c.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0 (Proposition 3.1). It is implied by WKL(w-bd) and WKL(ext-bd).

statement.name: WKL for trees with bounded width
statement.definition: An infinite binary tree T ⊆ 2^{<N} has a path if there is c such that |T^{=n}| ≤ c for all n.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL(ext-bd) over RCA0 (Theorem 3.2). Not provable in RCA0 (Corollary 3.4 and Theorem 3.3, which shows that if IΣ02 fails there is a counterexample). It is provable in RCA0 + IΣ02 (Lemma 2.2). It is implied by IΣ02 ∨ VSMALL (Proposition 3.7). Together with 'there is a set X computing every set' it implies IΣ02 (Corollary 3.6). Strictly between RCA0 and WKL0. Whether it is strictly weaker than IΣ02 ∨ VSMALL is left open (Question 3.2).

statement.name: WKL for trees with bounded number of extendible nodes per level
statement.definition: An infinite binary tree T ⊆ 2^{<N} has a path if there is c such that for every n, the number of extendible nodes of length n is at most c.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL(w-bd) over RCA0 (Theorem 3.2). Provable from IΣ02 (Lemma 2.2). Not provable in RCA0 (Corollary 3.4).

statement.name: Σ01-WKL for bounded prefix-free subsets
statement.definition: An infinite Σ01 binary tree has a path if prefix-free subsets of the tree are bounded in size by some c.
statement.facts: Equivalent to BΣ02 and to KL(pf-bd) over RCA0 (Theorem 2.1).

statement.name: Σ01-WKL for bounded width (Chaitin's lemma)
statement.definition: An infinite Σ01 binary tree has a path if |T^{=n}| ≤ c for all n.
statement.facts: Equivalent to IΣ02 and to KL(w-bd) over RCA0 (Theorem 2.3).

statement.name: Σ01-WKL for bounded extendible nodes
statement.definition: An infinite Σ01 binary tree has a path if the number of extendible nodes of each length is bounded by some c.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 and to KL(ext-bd) over RCA0 (Corollary 1.2, using Proposition 1.1).

statement.name: König's lemma with bounded prefix-free subsets
statement.definition: An infinite tree T ⊆ N^{<N} has a path if prefix-free subsets of T are bounded in size by some c.
statement.facts: Equivalent to BΣ02 and to Σ01-WKL(pf-bd) over RCA0 (Theorem 2.1).

statement.name: König's lemma with bounded width
statement.definition: An infinite tree T ⊆ N^{<N} has a path if |T^{=n}| ≤ c for all n.
statement.facts: Equivalent to IΣ02 and to Σ01-WKL(w-bd) over RCA0 (Theorem 2.3).

statement.name: König's lemma with bounded extendible nodes
statement.definition: A finitely branching infinite tree T ⊆ N^{<N} has a path if the number of extendible nodes of each length is bounded by some c.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 and to Σ01-WKL(ext-bd) over RCA0 (Corollary 1.2).

statement.name: WKL variants producing recursive paths
statement.definition: An infinite binary tree T ⊆ 2^{<N} has a T-recursive path if the width, respectively the number of extendible nodes per level, is bounded by some c.
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to IΣ02 over RCA0.

statement.name: Very smallness (Binns–Kjos-Hanssen)
statement.definition: An infinite binary tree has a path if for every function f there is n such that for all m ≥ n, the number of extendible nodes of length f(m) is below m.
statement.facts: IΣ02 ∨ VSMALL implies WKL(w-bd) over RCA0 (Proposition 3.7).

statement.name: Well-partial-orderedness of the tree structure T(B(·)) (binary trees with embeddability, order-isomorphic to Friedman's T2)
statement.definition: The partial order of generalized trees built from binary trees B(·), with maximal order type the Howard-Bachmann ordinal ϑ(ε_{Ω+1}). The statement is that this order is a wpo.
statement.facts: ACA0 proves 'T(B(·)) is a wpo' → WF(ϑ(ε_{Ω+1})) (Thm 6.1). Hence ACA0 + (Π11-CA0)^- does not prove 'T(B(·)) is a wpo' (Thm 6.2). For each n, ACA0 + (Π11-CA0)^- proves 'T(·^{*...*}) (n stars) is a wpo' (Thm 6.4).

statement.name: Lightface Π11 comprehension and its Π03 restriction
statement.definition: Comprehension for formulas ∀X B(X) with B Π0n (or arbitrary arithmetical B) containing no free set parameters, only numerical parameters.
statement.facts: |RCA0 + (Π11(Π03)-CA0)^-| = ϑ(Ω^ω) = |Π12-BI0|. |RCA0* + (Π11(Π03)-CA0)^-| ≥ ϕ_ω 0. |ACA0 + (Π11-CA0)^-| = ϑ(ε_{Ω+1}). RCA0 + (Π11(Π02)-CA0)^- has ordinal |IΣ3|. RCA0* + (Π11(Π02))^- is Π4-conservative over IΣ2. RCA0 + (Π11(Π03)-CA0)^- does not prove 'T(X*) is a wpo'.

statement.name: Existence of an idempotent non-principal ultrafilter on N (higher-order)
statement.definition: There is a non-principal ultrafilter U on N, formalized as an object of type N^N → N in higher-order arithmetic, with U = U + U. Equivalently, X ∈ U implies {n | X − n ∈ U} ∈ U.
statement.facts: Theorem 7: RCA_0^ω ⊢ (U_idem) → (µ) ∧ IHT. Theorem 9: ACA_0^ω + (µ) + IHT + (U_idem) is Π^1_2-conservative over ACA_0 + IHT, hence over ACA_0^+ and over ACA_0. Theorem 10: program extraction for Π^1_2 theorems of this system, giving a term of T_1[µ]. This is optimal: (U_idem) cannot be Π^1_2-conservative over a system not containing IHT. Remark 19: the results also hold for idempotent ultrafilters on countable semigroups.

statement.name: Existence of a non-principal ultrafilter (higher-order)
statement.definition: There is a non-principal ultrafilter on N, given by an object U of type N^N → N.

statement.name: Special fan functional
statement.definition: A functional Θ of type 2→1* such that for all G^2 and f≤1 there is g in Θ(G) with f in [gG(g)]; it computes a finite subcover of Cantor space from a canonical cover. Equivalent to HBU (Cousin's lemma) over ACA^ω_0+QF-AC^{2,1}.
statement.facts: Not computable from any type two functional. Computable from ∃^3. RCA^ω_0+(∃Θ)SFF(Θ) is conservative over RCA_0+WKL. For any Θ some hyperarithmetical G has Θ(G) non-hyperarithmetical. Θ together with µ^2 computes a realiser for ATR0 but not uniformly the Suslin functional S^2 (only hyperarithmetical functions are uniformly computable from Θ and µ). µ^1+Θ proves Π^1_1-TR0; Π^1_1-CA^ω_0+QF-AC+HBU proves ∆^1_2-CA0 and the Π^1_3 consequences of Π^1_2-CA0.

statement.name: Regressive Hindman's Theorem

statement.facts: Implies RT^1 (Lemma 3), HT (Proposition 5) and λregHT[ap] (Proposition 4, strongly Weihrauch). It follows from canHT (Proposition 3).

statement.name: Bounded λ-regressive Hindman's Theorems with apartness

statement.facts: For n >= 2, λregHT^{=n}[ap] is equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorems 3 and 4). It satisfies λregHT^{=n}[ap] ≥W RAN, ≥W WOP(X -> ω^X), ≥c HT^{=n}_k[ap] and ≥c IPT^2_2, and ≤sW regRT^n. RT^3_3 ≰c λregHT^{=2}[ap].

statement.name: Kanamori–McAloon Regressive Ramsey's Theorem

statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 for n >= 2 (Theorem 1). RT^n_k ≤c regRT^n (Proposition 7). RT^{2n-1}_2 ≥sW regRT^n (Hirst). regRT^n ≰c RT^n_k (Corollary 3).

statement.name: Canonical Ramsey's Theorem (Erdős–Rado)
statement.definition: For every c : [N]^n -> N there is an infinite canonical set H and S ⊆ {1..n} such that c(I) = c(J) iff I and J agree on S.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 for n >= 2 (Theorem 1). It implies RT^n and regRT^n.

statement.name: Hindman-type theorems with apartness
statement.definition: Hindman's Theorem (possibly restricted to sums of exactly or at most n terms) with the apartness condition on the solution set.
statement.facts: HT ≥sW HT[ap] (Corollary 1). HT^{=2}_2[ap] is strictly weaker than ACA0 (follows from RT^2_2). HT^{=n}_k[ap] is equivalent to ACA0 for n >= 3, k >= 2 (cited from [5]).

statement.name: Well-ordering preservation principle for base-ω exponentiation

statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 (Girard, Hirst). WOP(X -> ω^X) ≤W λregHT^{=n}[ap] for n >= 2 (Theorem 6). It is also ≤W RT^3_3 (cited from [7]) and claimed ≤W HT^{=3}_2[ap].

statement.name: Alternative definitions of well-quasi-order
statement.definition: wqo(set): every f:N→Q has an infinite non-decreasing subsequence set. wqo(anti): no infinite descending sequence and no infinite antichain. wqo(ext): every linear extension is a well-order.
statement.facts: Over RCA0 wqo(set) implies wqo, and wqo implies wqo(anti) and wqo(ext). No other implication holds in REC. WKL0 proves wqo(ext) implies wqo. 'Every wqo(anti) is wqo(set)' is equivalent to CAC. 'Every wqo is wqo(set)' implies RT^1_<∞. 'Every finite quasi-order is wqo(set)' is equivalent to RT^1_<∞. 'Every well-order is wqo(set)' is equivalent to ADS.

statement.name: Better-quasi-order and variants
statement.definition: Every f from a barrier (or block) into Q is good. bqo(set) asks for a subbarrier on which f is perfect.
statement.facts: WKL0 proves bqo implies bqo(block). 'Every bqo is bqo(set)' is equivalent to ATR0 (Theorem 3.9). 'n is bqo(set)' is equivalent to ATR0 for n ≥ 2. Closure of bqo under disjoint union, intersection and product implies ACA0 and is provable in ATR0. The strength of '3 is bqo' is open.

statement.name: Kruskal's tree theorem for labelled trees

statement.facts: Provable in Π^1_1-CA0 and in Towsner's Σ2-LPP0. Implies ATR0 (Theorem 6.12). The unlabelled statement is not provable in ATR0 (Friedman).

statement.name: Laver's theorem (linear orders are bqo)

statement.name: Product of wqos is wqo

statement.name: Young diagrams wqo

statement.name: Strong weak weak Kőnig's lemma
statement.loc: Section 1 (Strong weak weak Kőnig's lemma) and Section 6
statement.definition: If T ⊆ 2^{<ω} is a tree of positive measure, then there is a nonempty subtree S ⊆ T such that for every σ ∈ S, S has positive measure above σ. It corresponds to the strong continuous covering property.
statement.facts: RCA0 + WKL ⊢ SWWKL (Prop. 6.1). SWWKL implies WSWWKL; the converse is open. Over RCA0, SWWKL does not imply WKL (Prop. 6.5), via an ω-model with no set of PA degree. Both SWWKL and WSWWKL lie strictly between WKL and WWKL over RCA0. SWWKL implies that every closed set of positive measure has a perfect subset of positive measure, which strengthens Patey's result that 'every closed set of positive measure has a perfect subset' does not imply WKL.

statement.name: Weak strong weak weak Kőnig's lemma
statement.definition: If T ⊆ 2^{<ω} is a tree of positive measure, then there is a subtree S ⊆ T of positive measure with no dead ends. It corresponds to the continuous covering property.
statement.facts: RCA0 + WSWWKL ⊢ WWKL (Prop. 6.2). RCA0 + WWKL does not prove WSWWKL (Prop. 6.3), shown by an ω-model of incomplete ML-randoms. It is implied by SWWKL and therefore by WKL. Whether it implies SWWKL is open.

statement.name: Jordan decomposition on the rationals
statement.definition: Instances are continuous functions f on [0,1] of bounded variation. Solutions are Jordan decompositions (g,h) of f restricted to the rationals in [0,1].
statement.facts: JDQ is Weihrauch equivalent to AMD (Prop. 2.12). JDQ is strongly Weihrauch equivalent to JDQ2, its dyadic version (Lemma 2.16). Any oracle computing Jordan decompositions on the rationals of a suitable computable function has PA degree (Cor. 2.13). There is no uniform way to compute a DNC_k function from such decompositions (Cor. 2.14).

statement.name: Atomless martingale domination
statement.definition: Instances are lower semicontinuous presentations of atomless martingales M. Solutions are martingales majorizing M.
statement.facts: AMD is Weihrauch equivalent to JDQ (Prop. 2.12). PJDQ2 and JDQ2 are strongly Weihrauch reducible to AMD and AMD is strongly Weihrauch reducible to JDQ2 (Prop. 2.18, 2.21).

statement.notation: FVP for continuous f and compact X
statement.name: Free variational principle for continuous potentials on compact spaces (also on Cantor space or [0,1])
statement.definition: Every continuous potential f: X → R≥0 on a compact complete separable metric space has an ε-critical point.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL₀ over RCA₀ (Proposition 7.4 and Proposition 9.1). The same holds for the Cantor space or [0,1] in place of general compact X.

statement.name: Free variational principle for continuous potentials
statement.definition: Every continuous potential on a complete separable metric space has an ε-critical point.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA₀ over RCA₀ (Theorem 7.5 and Proposition 9.2); it is enough to take the Baire space.

statement.name: Free variational principle on compact spaces
statement.definition: Every lower semi-continuous potential on a compact complete separable metric space has an ε-critical point.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA₀ over RCA₀ (Theorem 8.2 and Proposition 9.3); it is enough to take [0,1].

statement.notation: LVP for compact X; LVP for continuous f and compact X
statement.name: Localized variational principle on compact spaces / for continuous potentials on compact spaces
statement.definition: The localized variational principle (the critical point x* also satisfies εd(x0,x*) ≤ f(x0) − f(x*)) restricted to compact X, resp. to continuous f on compact X.
statement.facts: Both are equivalent to ACA₀ over RCA₀. It is enough to take X = [0,1] or X = [0,1]×[0,1] with the max metric.

statement.name: Localized variational principle for continuous potentials
statement.definition: The localized variational principle restricted to continuous potentials on complete separable metric spaces.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Π¹₁-CA₀ over RCA₀. It is enough to take X to be the closed unit ball of C[0,1]. The principle is also equivalent to Π¹₁-CA₀ when f is bounded (Proposition 10.12).

statement.name: Σ¹₁ axiom of choice (as base theory)

statement.facts: Used as the base theory for the incompleteness theorems. No Σ¹₁-AC₀ facts relating catalogue statements are proved. The paper shows that Π¹₁-sound Σ¹₁-definable extensions of Σ¹₁-AC₀ do not prove their own Π¹₁-soundness.

statement.name: Stable fallow Erdős–Moser theorem for finitely many colors
statement.definition: For any k and any stable k-coloring c (limy c(x,y) exists for each x), there is an infinite set A on which c is fallow, that is, c(x,z) ∈ {c(x,y), c(y,z)} for all x<y<z in A.
statement.facts: IΣ^0_2 proves the ≪2-basis theorem for sEM_{<∞} (Theorem 3.5, whose proof reduces EM_{<∞} to this case). RCA0 + IΣ^0_2 proves COH + sEM_{<∞} → EM_{<∞}.

statement.name: Complementation theorem for parity tree automata
statement.definition: For every nondeterministic parity tree automaton A there is a tree automaton B such that for any tree T, B accepts T iff A does not accept T.
statement.facts: Equivalent over ACA0 to positional determinacy of all almost tree-like parity games (Thm 3.2). Implied over ACA0 by positional determinacy of all parity games and implies ∀x[(Σ02)x-Det] (Cor 3.3). Provable in Π13-CA0 but not in Δ13-CA0. Over Π12-CA0 equivalent to positional determinacy of parity games, ∀x[(Σ02)x-Det], decidability of the Π13 MSO theory of the binary tree, and RFN_Π13(Π12-CA0) (Thm 6.3).

statement.name: Determinacy of all Boolean combinations of Σ02 Gale-Stewart games (difference hierarchy)
statement.definition: The scheme asserting that for every x all (Σ02)x Gale-Stewart games are determined; (Σ02)x-Det* is the Cantor-space version.
statement.facts: Equivalent in ACA0 to the Cantor-space version (Prop 2.11) and to positional determinacy of tree-like parity games (Lemma 2.13). Provable from ACA0 + Δ12-MI + Σ13-IND, hence from Π13-CA0, but not from Δ13-CA0 (Cor 4.3). Π12-CA0 proves (Σ02)n-Det for each n in ω. Over ACA0 the theory {(Σ02)n-Det : n in ω} axiomatizes the Π13 consequences of Π12-CA0 (Thm 6.1). Equivalent over Π12-CA0 to the other principles in Thm 6.3.

statement.notation: Positional determinacy of all parity games
statement.name: Positional determinacy of parity games
statement.definition: Every parity game G=<V∃,V∀,vI,E,rk> has a positional (memoryless) winning strategy for one of the players.
statement.facts: Π12-CA0 proves it for index (0,n) for each n and the step (0,x) to (0,x+1) (Lemma 4.6). Implies the complementation theorem over ACA0 (Cor 3.3). Not provable in Δ13-CA0. Equivalent over Π12-CA0 to the other statements in Thm 6.3.

statement.name: Decidability of the Π1n MSO theory of the infinite binary tree
statement.definition: There is a Turing machine halting on all inputs that accepts exactly the Π1n sentences of MSO true in ({0,1}*,S0,S1).
statement.facts: ACA0 proves positional determinacy of all parity games implies (2n) for every n in ω. Over Π12-CA0, (2n) for n>=3 implies ∀x[(Σ02)x-Det]. Equivalent over Π12-CA0 for n=3 to the statements in Thm 6.3. Hence unprovable in Δ13-CA0.

statement.name: Π13 reflection principle for Π12-CA0
statement.definition: Every Π13 sentence provable in Π12-CA0 is true: ∀φ∈Π13 [Pr(φ) ⇒ Tr(φ)].
statement.facts: Implies Con(Π12-CA0), thus unprovable in Π12-CA0. Equivalent over Π12-CA0 to positional determinacy of parity games, ∀x[(Σ02)x-Det], complementation for tree automata and decidability of the Π13 MSO theory of the binary tree.

statement.name: Second-order arithmetic subsystems (Π1n/Δ1n comprehension, Δ12 monotone inductive definitions, Σ12 choice)
statement.definition: Comprehension for Π1n (resp. Δ1n) formulas; Σ12-AC the Σ12 axiom of choice; Δ12-MI existence of least fixed points of Δ12 monotone operators.
statement.facts: Π12-CA0 proves Σ12-AC (Thm 2.2) and Δ12-MI (Thm 2.6) and the existence of β2-models (Thm 2.4). Δ13-CA0 is Π14-conservative over Π12-CA0 and does not prove ∀x[(Σ02)x-Det]. Not catalogue statements.

statement.name: Minimal bad sequence lemma
statement.definition: For a quasi-ordering and a well-founded relation compatible with it, every bad sequence is bounded below by a minimal bad sequence.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Π¹₁-CA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 2.3, from Simpson–Marcone [26]).

statement.name: Locally minimal bad array lemma
statement.definition: Version of the minimal bad array lemma for arrays on barriers, with locally minimal bad arrays.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Π¹₁-CA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 2.22, from [26]).

statement.name: Minimal bad array lemma
statement.definition: Generalization of the minimal bad sequence lemma to arrays indexed by barriers.
statement.facts: Provable in Π¹₂-CA0 by a crude analysis; its exact strength is open (Problem 2.19), conjectured not provable in Π¹₁-CA0.

statement.name: Kruskal's theorem (and generalized version)
statement.definition: Finite trees are wqo under homeomorphic embedding; generalized version for labelled trees with wqo labels.
statement.facts: Provable in Π¹₁-CA0 and not provable in ATR0 (Theorem 2.10, Friedman).

statement.name: Graph minor theorem
statement.definition: The minor ordering on finite graphs is wqo.
statement.facts: Not provable in Π¹₁-CA0 (Theorem 2.13, Friedman–Robertson–Seymour).

statement.name: Barrier theorem
statement.definition: If B is a barrier and f : B → {0,1}, then there is a subbarrier B' ⊆ B on which f is constant.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0, and to the statement that for bqo Q every map from a barrier has a perfect restriction on a subbarrier (Theorem 4.9).

statement.name: Wqo preserved by finite power set under ∃∀ ordering
statement.definition: If Q is wqo then the set of finite subsets of Q is wqo with respect to the ∃∀ quasi-ordering.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RT22.

statement.notation: closure of bqo under product, disjoint union, intersection of orderings
statement.name: Lemma 5.16 statements
statement.definition: Product of bqos is bqo; disjoint union of bqos is bqo; a bqo under two orderings is bqo under their intersection.
statement.facts: Equivalent to each other over RCA0; each implies ACA0 (Lemma 5.17) and is provable in ATR0; conjectured equivalent to ATR0 (Conjecture 5.18).

statement.name: Every wqo sequence has an increasing subsequence
statement.definition: If a quasi-ordering is wqo then every sequence has an infinite subset on which it is nondecreasing.
statement.facts: Provable in RT22 and implies RT1<∞ over RCA0; conjectured equivalent to RT22 (Conjecture 4.3).

statement.name: The antichain with three elements is bqo
statement.definition: The 3-element antichain is a better quasi-order.
statement.facts: Provable in ATR0 and not known to be provable in any weaker subsystem (open Problem 3.3); if a theory proves it then it proves that every finite antichain is bqo (Theorem 5.11).

statement.name: Browder-Göhde-Kirk theorem (realiser problem)
statement.definition: Given a nonexpansive self-map f of a nonempty, co-semi-decidable, computably overt, bounded, convex subset K of a uniformly convex computable Banach space, output a fixed point of f.
statement.facts: BGK_[0,1] ≡_W IVT ≡_W BFT_1 (Prop. 3.21). BGK on the unit ball of l2 is ≡_W lim (Cor. 5.10). BGK on the Hilbert cube is ≡_W WKL (Thm 5.14). In Hilbert space BGK_K ≡_W ConvC_K^{w→n} (Thm 5.8). BGK_K ≤_W Proj_K ≤_W lim∘lim, and ≤_W lim for K computably compact or H Hilbert space. In finite dimension BGK is strictly below WKL, and every computable instance has a computable fixed point (Cor. 3.11). In infinite dimension there are computable firmly nonexpansive maps on the Hilbert cube with no computable fixed point (Thm 3.15).

statement.name: Projection onto the fixed point set
statement.definition: Given a nonexpansive f : K → K and x in K, output the metric projection of x onto Fix(f).
statement.facts: Proj_[0,1] ≡_W lim (Prop. 3.20). BGK_K ≤_W Proj_K (Prop. 3.5). Proj_K ≤_W lim in uniformly convex, uniformly smooth spaces (Thm 6.10) and ≤_W lim∘lim in general (Prop. 3.8).

statement.name: Limit problem and rate-of-convergence problem of a fixed point iteration I
statement.definition: Given f and a starting point x, output the limit of the iteration I(f,x), respectively a rate of convergence for it.
statement.facts: BGK_K ≤_W lim(I) ≤_W Conv_I ≤_W lim (Prop. 3.5). For projective, or simple and retractive, or avoidant I on [0,1], lim(I) ≡_W Conv_I ≡_W lim (Prop. 3.20).

statement.name: Weak-to-strong and weak-to-weak closed choice on K (convex and unique variants)
statement.definition: Closed choice on a weakly closed set (given by negative information in the weak topology), with output in the strong or weak topology. The Conv variant is restricted to convex sets and the UC variant to singletons.
statement.facts: BGK_K ≡_W ConvC_K^{w→n} and WBGK_K ≡_W ConvC_K^{w→w} (Thm 5.8). On the unit ball of l2, UC^{w→n} ≡_W ConvC^{w→n} ≡_W lim (Cor. 5.10), while UC^{n→n} is equivalent to C_{N^N}. On a computably compact K these coincide with ConvC_K.

statement.name: Weak Browder-Göhde-Kirk theorem
statement.definition: Like BGK_K, but the fixed point need only be computed in the weak topology.
statement.facts: WBGK ≡_W ConvC_K^{w→w} (Thm 5.8). WBGK_{B_l2} ≡_W WKL, by the proof of Thm 5.14.

statement.name: Generalized weak König's lemma for Φ_n- and Ψ_n-trees
statement.definition: WKL extended from quantifier-free binary trees to trees whose predicate A(k) is a Φ_n formula (resp. Ψ_n formula): n alternating bounded function quantifiers, starting with a universal (resp. existential) one, in front of a Π⁰₁ formula, with parameters of arbitrary finite type. Φ_∞-WKL is the union over n.
statement.facts: Over the finite-type systems E-G_kA^ω (k≥3), E-PRA^ω and E-PA^ω, Φ_0-WKL, Ψ_0-WKL and the parameter-restricted versions Φ⁻_m-WKL and Ψ⁻_n-WKL are all equivalent to WKL (Proposition 5.7). With higher-type parameters the principles form a non-collapsing hierarchy. Φ_{n+1}-WKL proves Π^{1,b}_n-comprehension (Proposition 5.11). Φ_1-WKL is not provable in E-PA^ω+QF-AC^{1,0}+QF-AC^{0,1}+µ (Proposition 5.13). Φ_n-WKL and Ψ_n-WKL for n≥2 are underivable there.

statement.name: Strengthened generalized weak König's lemma
statement.definition: The form ∀h ∃a ∃f≤1 ∀ñ≤h(a) A(a,fñ) → ∃a ∃f≤1 ∀n A(a,fn), with A in Φ_n (resp. Ψ_n) and arbitrary parameters.
statement.facts: Φ_n-WKL⁺ implies Φ_n-WKL. Φ_0-WKL⁺ is equivalent to Φ_0-WKL over T+QF-AC^{0,0} (Proposition 5.17). T+QF-AC^{1,0}+F⁻ proves Φ_∞-WKL⁺ (Proposition 6.1). E-PRA^ω+QF-AC^{1,0}+QF-AC^{0,1}+Φ_∞-WKL⁺ is Π⁰₂-conservative over PRA (Theorem 7.2), with analogous conservation results over EA and PA. Ψ_1-WKL⁺ suffices to prove a modulus of uniform continuity for directly represented continuous functions.

statement.name: Uniform Σ⁰₁-boundedness
statement.definition: A non-standard schema of uniform boundedness for Σ⁰₁ formulas over bounded function quantifiers in all finite types.
statement.facts: E-G_3A^ω+Σ⁰₁-UB proves WKL (Proposition 3.3). Σ⁰₁-UB yields moduli of uniform continuity (Proposition 3.4) and proves every Φ_n-WKL⁺. The theories with Σ⁰₁-UB are Π⁰₂-conservative over EA and PRA, and conservative over PA (Theorem 7.1).

statement.name: Non-standard axiom F
statement.definition: A non-standard bounding axiom: for all Φ and y there is y₀≤y with Φkz ≤ Φk(y₀k) for all k and all z≤yk. It fails in the full set-theoretic model.
statement.facts: E-G_3A^ω+QF-AC^{1,0}+F⁻ proves F (Proposition 3.6). T+QF-AC^{1,0}+F proves Σ⁰₁-UB (Proposition 3.2). A rule for extracting closed terms holds for T+QF-AC^{1,0}+QF-AC^{0,1}+F (Theorem 3.7).

statement.name: Pigeonhole principle for Σ⁰ₙ formulas
statement.definition: For every Σ⁰ₙ formula φ(x) there is an infinite set H such that either ∀x∈H φ(x) or ∀x∈H ¬φ(x).
statement.facts: Σ⁰ₙ₊₁-Subset has a weakly lowₙ basis and a lowₙ₊₁ basis (Main Theorem 1.6, Cor. 6.1, Thm 6.26). Over RCA₀, Σ⁰ₙ-Subset does not imply Δ⁰ₙ₊₁-Subset (Cor. 6.2, via ω-models). Δ⁰ₙ₊₁-Subset does not imply Σ⁰ₙ₊₁-Subset (Cor. 7.2), so the hierarchy Σ⁰₁ < Δ⁰₂ < Σ⁰₂ < Δ⁰₃ < … is strict (Main Theorem 1.9). RCA₀+IΣ⁰ₙ+Σ⁰ₙ-Subset is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀+IΣ⁰ₙ for n ≥ 2 (Main Theorem 1.10). Σ⁰₂-Subset does not preserve hyperimmunity at levels {0,1}. Whether Σ⁰₂-Subset is Π¹₁-conservative over BΣ⁰₂ is open.

statement.name: Pigeonhole principle for Δ⁰ₙ formulas
statement.definition: For Σ⁰ₙ φ and Π⁰ₙ ψ with ∀x(φ↔ψ), there is an infinite H with ∀x∈H φ(x) or ∀x∈H ¬φ(x).
statement.facts: Δ⁰ₙ₊₁-Subset has no lowₙ basis [13] and a weakly lowₙ basis [34]. It preserves hyperimmunity at levels {n−2,n−1} (Main Theorem 1.8). RCA₀+Δ⁰ₙ₊₂-Subset is not Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀+BΣ⁰ₙ₊₁ (Prop. 8.15), e.g. Δ⁰₃-Subset is not Π¹₁-conservative over BΣ⁰₂. Only Δ⁰₂-Subset was matched to catalogue entry d22; its facts are listed under d22.

statement.name: Ginsburg–Sands theorem for T1-spaces
statement.definition: Every infinite T₁ topological space has an infinite subspace homeomorphic to the discrete or the cofinite topology on N.
statement.facts: RCA₀ ⊢ GST₁ ↔ COH + Σ⁰₂-Subset (Benham et al.). GST₁ admits a weakly low basis (Cor. 6.32). RCA₀+IΣ⁰₂+GST₁ is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀+IΣ⁰₂ (Cor. 8.14).
